title: MRO Corp Reviews 2026: AI-Powered Medical Record Retrieval for Law Firms
summary: MRO Corp reviews for 2026: what MRO's requester portal offers law firms, and how Codes Health compares with AI analysis and flat-fee pricing.
body_markdown:
For plaintiff law firms handling personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, and workers' compensation cases, medical record retrieval is still one of the most time-consuming parts of pre-litigation work. Slow provider responses, rejected authorizations, and incomplete record sets can hold up case evaluations, settlement negotiations, and trial preparation. MRO Corp is a release-of-information company that many law firms encounter when requesting records from hospitals and health systems. This review looks at what MRO offers legal requesters and how[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) , an AI-native retrieval and analysis platform built for plaintiff firms, compares.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


**MRO's legal-facing tools center on request management:** MRO's Requester Portal lets high-volume requesters submit, track, pay for, and receive records electronically from participating healthcare facilities.


-


**MRO's newest AI product isn't aimed at law firms:** Prodigy, launched in September 2026, is an AI engine for clinical registry abstraction at health systems, not an attorney-facing retrieval tool.


-


**Codes Health reports an average turnaround of a couple of weeks for complete records,** and verifies completeness before delivery.


-


**Authorization errors cause preventable delays:** Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests, and Codes Health's AI validation catches missing signatures, unclear expiration dates, and unchecked boxes before submission.


-


**Completeness checks reduce supplemental requests:** Codes Health's AI-powered completeness verification identifies gaps and missing facilities earlier, cutting down on avoidable back-and-forth.


-


**Litigation-focused insights go beyond raw records:** Codes Health flags potential breaches of care, documented future medical needs, and pre-existing conditions for attorney review.


-


**Integrated workflows reduce staff overhead:** Filevine users can request, track, and receive Codes Health records without leaving their case files, and high-volume firms can get custom integrations.


## **What MRO Corp Offers Law Firms**


MRO primarily serves healthcare providers such as hospitals, health systems, clinics, and practices, managing release-of-information operations on their behalf with a mix of remote and on-site staff. When your firm requests records from a facility that uses MRO, you're working with MRO as the facility's ROI vendor.


For attorneys and other high-volume requesters, MRO offers a Requester Portal with four main functions:


-


**eRequest:** Submit record requests electronically to participating healthcare facilities instead of by mail


-


**eStatus:** View the real-time status of requests to facilities in the MRO network, searchable by tracking number, facility, patient details, or your own reference number


-


**ePay:** Manage and confirm online credit card payments, including multiple transactions at once


-


**eDelivery:** View, save, or print requested records, with secure file transfer options for larger volumes


### **What Legal Teams Should Know About MRO**


-


**Coverage follows MRO's client facilities.** The portal handles requests to healthcare facilities in MRO's network. Cases that involve providers served by other ROI vendors, or no vendor at all, still need separate requests and follow-up.


-


**The AI focus is provider-side.** MRO launched Prodigy in September 2026 as an AI engine for clinical registry abstraction at health systems. The MRO materials reviewed for this article don't describe it as an attorney-facing retrieval or analysis tool.


-


**Analysis happens elsewhere.** MRO's public requester materials describe request submission, tracking, payment, and delivery. They don't describe litigation chronologies, breach-of-care flagging, or completeness review against a law firm's original request, so firms typically handle that work internally or through another vendor.


The key difference: MRO is a facility-side ROI vendor with a requester portal, while Codes Health works on the law firm's side across every provider in a case, then organizes and analyzes what comes back.


## **Understanding AI-Powered Medical Record Retrieval for Legal Practices**


Medical record retrieval has historically required significant paralegal and staff time. The traditional workflow involves:


-


Preparing and submitting authorization forms to providers


-


Following up via phone, fax, and email for status updates


-


Tracking multiple requests across spreadsheets or basic software


-


Reviewing returned records for completeness


-


Organizing thousands of pages into usable formats


-


Chasing missing records when gaps are identified


This manual approach creates operational drag that affects case timelines and staff capacity. Published turnaround times vary considerably by provider and request pathway, and when a case involves several providers, delays at any one of them can hold up the whole record set.


AI-native platforms address these bottlenecks by automating authorization validation, provider outreach, completeness verification, and record organization.

## **Understanding Release of Information (ROI) with Codes Health**


### **Streamlining Authorizations and Preventing Errors**


Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied medical record requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can force you to resubmit and start over. Common issues that trigger rejections include:


-


Missing patient signatures


-


Unclear or expired authorization dates


-


Unchecked boxes for sensitive records (mental health, substance abuse, HIV)


-


Misspelled provider names or incorrect facility information


-


Missing dates of service


A rejected authorization means resubmitting the request, and for cases with multiple providers, those preventable delays add up quickly. Applicable deadlines depend on the request type and jurisdiction. HIPAA's right of access generally gives covered entities 30 days to respond to an individual's request, with state variations, while attorney-authorized requests may follow different procedures.


[Codes Health's AI review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) catches these errors before submission. The system automatically flags misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections. It also checks requested date ranges and provider-specific requirements, so problems surface early rather than after weeks of waiting.


### **Secure and Compliant Document Management**


The platform provides HIPAA-compliant e-signature workflows for intake documents, including releases of information and authorization forms. Secure document storage supports continued access to retrieved materials and reduces duplicate work when the same records are relevant across different case stages.


All data handling follows HIPAA requirements for protected health information, with[AES-256 encryption](https://app.getcodeshealth.com/) at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit securing records throughout retrieval and storage.


## **Beyond Retrieval: AI-Powered Insights from Medical Records**


### **Automated Chronologies and Summaries**


Raw medical records, often thousands of pages per case, take substantial review time before they're useful for case strategy. Codes Health's[AI-powered case chronologies](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) automatically organize, compile, and summarize records chronologically, grouping patient encounters and bills by visit.


These chronologies help legal teams:


-


Identify treatment timelines without manual page-by-page review


-


Spot gaps in care documentation that may need additional retrieval


-


Prepare for depositions with organized medical histories


-


Support demand letter preparation with documented treatment progression


Document summaries condense individual records into key findings while keeping connections to source material for verification and expert review.


### **Extracting Actionable Insights for Legal Cases**


Codes Health goes beyond document retrieval by surfacing litigation-focused information such as potential breach-of-care indicators, documented future medical needs, pre-existing conditions, and treatment gaps:


-


**Breach-of-care indicators:** The platform flags potential departures from standard care for attorney and expert review


-


**Future medical expense extraction:** AI identifies documented future medical needs and costs in the records, supporting damages calculations


-


**Pre-existing condition identification:** Automatic flagging of documented prior conditions helps attorneys evaluate causation and damages arguments and prepare for defense challenges concerning prior injuries or conditions


-


**Missed appointment tracking:** Documentation gaps that might affect case value are surfaced during review


A copilot-style interface also lets users ask questions about a patient's history instead of searching every document.

## **Persistent Provider Follow-Up and Verified Completeness**


### **Ensuring Complete Record Sets**


Codes Health manages provider outreach across calls, faxes, emails, portals, and other available channels until requested materials arrive. The platform uses provider and facility data to help identify where records may exist, which is especially important for cases involving multiple treatment facilities, long medical histories, or incomplete client recollection.


Rather than simply delivering whatever records arrive, the platform performs[completeness verification](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) that compares returned materials with the original request and available patient history. This helps identify:


-


Missing facilities not included in initial requests


-


Missing date ranges that may contain relevant treatment


-


Absent billing records needed for damages calculations


-


Documentation gaps that could affect case value


### **Transparency in the Retrieval Process**


The firm gets visibility into completed outreach and next required actions instead of relying on periodic vendor updates or chasing providers manually. For Filevine users, this information is available inside the associated case project, so you can review completed work and outstanding items without requesting separate vendor updates.


## **HIPAA Compliance and Data Security**


Medical record retrieval involves handling sensitive protected health information across multiple parties. Codes Health operates as a[HIPAA-compliant platform](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) with security measures appropriate for legal workflows handling PHI, including role-based access, audit trails, and business associate agreements.


The platform retrieves records through claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone, giving firms broad coverage across the providers in a case.


For law firms concerned about[data privacy](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/private-policy) , the platform's compliance posture supports the confidentiality requirements built into attorney-client relationships and medical-legal documentation.


## **Competitive Landscape: How Modern Platforms Compare**


Medical record retrieval includes several categories of providers, each with its own approach:

-


**Established retrieval providers** vary in their security certifications and infrastructure. Lexitas, for example, documents SOC 2 controls for its legal technology and SOC 2 Type 2 certification for its Record Insights product.


-


**Record Retrieval Solutions** uses a published flat-fee retrieval model and also offers medical summaries and chronologies as additional services.


-


**AI-powered platforms** like Codes Health and Tavrn use automation to speed up retrieval and add analytical capabilities. Tavrn offers medical record retrieval, chronologies, and AI-generated demand letters, while Codes Health focuses on upstream case intelligence: potential breach-of-care flags, missing record identification, and future expense extraction that inform case strategy.


-


**Broad litigation support providers** like Lexitas offer record retrieval as part of wider legal support services, with more than 40 U.S. locations and additional capabilities like court reporting and process service.


Codes Health stands out through its combination of litigation-focused intelligence, a couple of weeks turnaround for complete records, flat fee pricing with chronologies and analysis included, and native Filevine integration. The platform is[backed by Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/codes-health) and was founded by graduates of MIT and Yale. Its MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, so the platform keeps evolving, improving, and becoming more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices.
